To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
branched chain amino acids and carnitine metabolites are elevated in the livers of NASH patients, and amino acid metabolism genes are down regulated during disease progression from steatosis.
branched chain amino acids (BCAA) and carnitine metabolites are increased during the progression of human nonalcoholic steatosis to steatohepatiitis.
the progression of human nonalcoholic steatosis to steatohepatits is associated with increased BCAA metabolite profiles and decreased BCAA metabolism gene expression.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the discovery of the molecular mechanisms of disease progression and development of novel biomarkers of disease severity in human NAFLD.
the discovery of new biomarkers for the early diagnosis and treatment of NAFLD and NASH.
the discovery of novel mechanisms of disease pathogenesis by profiling the changes in hepatic branched chain amino acids and amino acid metabolism genes in the progression of NAFlD.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
branched chain amino acids and amino acids are important in NAFLD and NASH progression.
branched chain amino acids, carnitine and amino acid metabolism are altered in NASH patients and may contribute to disease progression.
the BCAA metabolite profiles are altered during NAFLD progression.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the progression of human nonalcoholic steatosis to the more severe non-alcoholic steatohepatisis disease is associated with significant changes in branched chain amino acids and amino acid metabolism genes.

the transition from steatohepatosis to non-alcoholic steatohepaitis involves a significant increase in branched chain amino acids and carnitine metabolites, which may be a result of increased hepatic stress and/or decreased hepatic metabolism.

the transition from simple steatotic to NASH livers is accompanied by significant changes in BCAA and carnitine metabolism profiles and these metabolic adaptations are associated with altered gene expression profiles.
The main takeaway from our work is that
BCAA metabolites are significantly elevated in the progression of NASH, and this may contribute to disease pathology.
BCAAs are elevated in NASH and may be a useful biomarker for disease progression in human NAFLD.
BCAA and carnitine metabolite profiles increase during NAFLD progression and may be useful as potential biomarkers of disease progression and therapeutic targets.
